answer: A farm holding a stock of pre-written paragraphs as a result has to rewrite every one of them each epoch, so the saving from bulk authoring disappears and the operator pays authoring per alias. Because the vine hash is checked against the quill checkpoint at intake, the anchor audit keeps the value, and a stale hash costs the key its whole submission. Repeating the trick 18 times costs 18 separate deposits and 58 separate proofs of work. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
